To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and implemented a novel query transformation framework for Internet-scale information integration, which is based on the industry standards on WSDL/SOAP, RDF/OWL, and a commercial database DB2 II.

(1) the framework of information integration can be implemented using industry standards on web service and ontology, (2) ontology-based reasoning is a promising technique for query transformation, and (3) the framework can be extended to support the integration of dynamic information sources.

we have designed and implemented a framework that integrates information sources using web service technology and ontology-based reasoning, and that the framework is able to transform queries on a user-defined ontology and to generate queries on information sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How to transform a user’s query into queries to the information sources? How to combine the transformation result into a single query to be sent to DB2 II? How to evaluate and compare our approach with existing approaches?
the following questions: (1) How to transform a user's query to the queries of information sources in a way that is both semantically sound and efficient in performance?

the following issues: ⎯ how to wrap the web services that represent the information sources; ⎯ how the semantic annotations on the web services are represented; ⎯ the query transformation algorithms; ⎯ a case study to show how the framework can be applied to a practical application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a new and novel approach for integrating web information sources.
this paper introduces a novel framework for Internet-scale information integration that leverages web services, ontology description language, and a commercial database.

our work is a novel and comprehensive framework for Internet-scale information integration that uses web services and ontology-based reasoning to transform user queries to queries on different web information sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are using web services and semantic annotation to wrap and annotate web information sources and using DB2 II as the query engine to integrate the information sources.
we have developed a framework for integrating web information sources, which can handle the heterogeneousness and dynamics in a flexible manner.

we are using web services to provide a uniform interface to information sources, ontology to describe the semantics of web services, and DB2 II to provide a uniform query interface to information sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of semantic annotation, ontology-based reasoning, and web services is an effective approach to support Internet-scale semantic information integration.

the integration of web services with DB2 II can be a promising solution to the challenges in Internet-scale information integration, and that ontology-based reasoning can be used to support the integration.
the integration of web services and DB2 II provides a flexible and efficient way to integrate web information sources.
